J-06.name: Unclear / choppy tape is reported as unclear
J-06.notes: PROMOTED failing -> PASSING in iter-6 (full depth) — the FIFTH and final MVP tape state and the honest-uncertainty CRITICAL anti-goal, now positively demonstrated against a DRIVEN choppy stream (distinct from iter-5's honest-unclear-on-silence). Net-new provider work (confirmed by diff, not forward-carried notes): _chop_stream() authored + wired into stream() via 'elif SIM-CHOP' (it previously emitted ZERO events). NO classifier/config change (classifier.py + config.py byte-untouched, 0 diff lines — the spec's red-flag guard honored: chop reads unclear purely through the existing fallback + four gate preconditions). Chop shape constants (_CHOP_*) live in simulated.py as scenario DATA, not config (no-magic-numbers honored). Every TradeEvent carries Side.UNKNOWN — aggressor classification deferred to the engine (reinforces single-source-of-truth). Browser-verified on SIM-CHOP: amber 'Unclear' headline (text-amber-400 rgb(251,191,36), bar bg-amber-500 rgb(245,158,11), ~20% width, via getComputedStyle + base-selector probe, NOT eyeballed/grep), confidence 0.200 (== unclear_confidence, < reasonable_confidence 0.60 — warmed, not cold-start 0.10); UI asserts NO side and NO absorption; observation 'Mixed or weak evidence — no clear side in control'; Event Log 'No events yet' (no spurious transition — correct honest behavior); all Recent Trades 100.00 mixed BUY/SELL/UNKNOWN; 30s features buy_ratio 0.500 / sell_ratio 0.500 (<0.60), avg_spread 0.148 (>0.06), buy/sell impact 0.000, bid/ask refresh 0.118/0.103 (<0.55) — past EVERY gate precondition. KEYSTONE TESTS (I ran the suite: 61 passed): test_sim_chop_never_misfires_a_resolved_state_step_through (state is STATE_UNCLEAR and NOT any of the four resolved states at EVERY tick over 600 events, cold AND warm), test_sim_chop_all_windows_deny_every_gate (every window incl. noise-prone 10s: both ratios < floor, spread > max_stable, both refresh < floor, impact past neither cutoff), test_sim_chop_settles_on_unclear (warm, event_count >= 40, conf == 0.20, no transition line), test_sim_chop_is_deterministic. Coherence PASS. Evidence: TC-10-sim-chop-unclear.png, UT-02-sim-chop-fullpage.png, UT-03-sim-chop-amber-features.png.

J-09.name: Stop watching a ticker
J-09.notes: Still FAILING — the LAST remaining Must-have journey (8 of 9 now passing). Re-confirmed failing iter-6 by diff inspection: apps/frontend was byte-untouched (0 diff lines), so no Stop / DELETE /watch UI control exists in the cockpit yet (explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for iter-6; the dev handoff names J-09 as the suggested next phase). The stream-status-dot groundwork landed iter-5 (top-bar dot reads canonical snapshot.stream_status). NEW concrete gotcha surfaced this iter (directly informs J-09 verification): the live -> idle teardown can only be observed on a still-LIVE stream, but (a) bounded sim streams run to exhaustion and watch() returns the EXISTING closed engine on re-watch, and (b) the harness PERMISSION LAYER blocks a backend restart (the browser-qa-agent tried and was denied). So J-09's teardown verification must arrange a fresh-backend / fresh-ticker observation, or use the new DELETE /watch endpoint itself to tear down a live engine. Remaining work: add the Stop control wired to DELETE /watch/{ticker} (verify the endpoint exists by code inspection per lesson iter-4), assert the stream closes + cockpit returns to idle/empty + re-watching starts a fresh read.
